project: Relay: AI Agent Job Orchestration Platform

criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.

stories.notes: Verified manually in-browser per the story's own Step 2/3 instructions (no automated test suite specified for the Command Center): all 9 tabs reachable, every card/bar drills down one level (Overview summary cards, role cards, system cards, release Gantt bars, and story rows all link to a real detail view), Sample vs Real mode verified on Overview with the sample badge visible only in Sample mode, plan/progress/manifest read at runtime via fetch (no hard-coded plan content), and the Data-as-of stamp renders on every page. Fixed a real timezone bug found during review: date-only fields (due_on, build_start, etc.) were rendering one day early in negative-UTC-offset zones because toLocaleDateString had no timeZone option; added timeZone: "UTC" to formatDateOrUnset and formatDataAsOf. Guardrails and Outcomes tabs show honest empty states (no SAFE-typed requirement, no measures defined yet) per the brief's own instruction to raise that gap rather than invent content.

criteria.text: Given a job in the queue, When it is processed, Then it is logged with a correlation ID
Given a re-delivered job, When it is processed, Then it does not double-process
Trust: All job processing is logged with correlation IDs

stories.notes: processJob() logs job_received then job_processed/job_skipped_duplicate/job_failed, every line carrying the caller's correlation ID (REQ-005). Idempotency via an atomic InMemoryIdempotencyStore.claim() (REQ-002) - a re-delivered job with the same idempotency key returns skipped_duplicate rather than reprocessing, verified even when the job id differs. Failure paths covered: a throwing store returns status failed and logs job_failed with an error class; a circular log context is caught by the logger itself rather than crashing job processing. 15/15 tests passing, tsc --noEmit clean. In-memory only - STORY-002 swaps in the real Redis Streams/SQS-backed store behind the same IdempotencyStore interface, not built here per the story's own scope note.

criteria.text: Given a job is submitted, When it is processed, Then it is logged with its correlation ID
Given a job is processed, When it is low-confidence, Then it is logged with its correlation ID
Trust: Given a job is processed, Then its processing is logged for traceability

stories.notes: RedisStreamQueue wraps real Redis Streams (XADD/XGROUP/XREADGROUP/XACK) via ioredis, run locally through docker-compose.yml - no AWS credentials available so SQS was not an option, Redis Streams satisfies REQ-001's either/or. dequeueOne() logs job_dequeued with the correlation ID (criterion 1) and, when job.confidence is below a placeholder threshold, job_low_confidence with the same correlation ID (criterion 2, REQ-011). Tests run against the actual Redis container, not mocked, including a real broken-connection failure path. Found and fixed two real bugs in review: ioredis emits its own console.error on an unhandled connection error (was doubling the failure-path test's assertion until an error listener was attached), and a default `import Redis from "ioredis"` fails strict tsc under Node16 module resolution even though tsx/vitest accepted it silently - switched to the named import. 22/22 tests passing, tsc --noEmit clean. Follow-up: added src/endToEnd.test.ts, composing queue.ts with STORY-001's processJob.ts against the real Redis container - proves enqueue -> dequeue -> idempotency check -> log works as one flow, including a re-delivered job producing exactly one job_processed and one job_skipped_duplicate with a consistent correlation ID. 25/25 tests passing now.

criteria.text: Given an API call is made, When the circuit breaker is closed, Then the call proceeds
Given an API call is made, When the circuit breaker is open, Then the call is blocked
Trust: Given output is generated, Then it is validated against the JSON schema before persisting

stories.notes: circuitBreaker.ts/withReliability.ts ported from CoreOps's proven mcp-server/src/reliability/ pattern (closed/open/half-open state machine, sliding failure window, timeout+backoff retry). persistOutput.ts gives the existing guardrails/outputContractGuardrail.ts its first real caller - validates before persisting (REQ-012), refuses to persist on any violation. callExternalApiAndPersist composes both: closed breaker lets the call proceed (criterion 1), open breaker blocks it fail-fast without invoking the call (criterion 2), and whatever the call returns is validated before persisting (criterion 3/trust) - tested as one composed flow, not just each piece alone. 48/48 tests passing, tsc --noEmit clean. src/tsconfig.json's rootDir changed to '..' with guardrails/outputContractGuardrail.ts added to include, matching the exact cross-package relative-import pattern CoreOps's mcp-server already uses for its own guardrails. Limitation: never exercised against a real external API, only a mock apiCall in tests - no real integration target exists in this project yet.

criteria.text: Given a job, When retries are exhausted, Then it is moved to the dead-letter queue
Given a dead-letter queue, When a job is triaged, Then it is logged with a reason
Trust: Dead-letter queue entries are logged with correlation IDs

stories.notes: dlq.ts reuses RedisStreamQueue (STORY-002) pointed at a separate DLQ stream - moveToDeadLetterQueue() preserves the original job payload alongside the failure reason and timestamp; triageNextDeadLetterEntry() reads it back and logs job_triaged with the reason. Wired into callExternalApiAndPersist: a job whose retries are genuinely exhausted (UpstreamCallFailedError) moves to the DLQ (criterion 1); a circuit-open rejection deliberately does NOT, since the call was never attempted - verified both directions against the real Redis DLQ stream. docs/runbooks/DLQ_TRIAGE.md written: what lands here and why, how to check it, a decision table by failure reason, when to escalate rather than guess, and an honest list of what it doesn't cover yet (no automated retry, no alerting, no UI). 55/55 tests passing, tsc --noEmit clean, STORY-003's original tests unaffected (dlqOptions is optional, backward compatible).

criteria.text: Given the system, When jobs are processed, Then SLO metrics are updated live
Given the SLO dashboard, When an error occurs, Then it is reflected in the error budget
Trust: SLO metrics are logged with correlation IDs

stories.notes: MetricsCollector tracks success rate, p95 latency, and a real error budget over a rolling count-based window (REQ-006) - wired into processJob.ts so it updates from real job outcomes (criterion 1), with an immediate reflection of any failure in the error budget (criterion 2), every recorded metric logged with its correlation ID (trust). dashboardServer.ts + dashboard.html serve a live dashboard (REQ-018) verified running in the browser, not just by test - watched it update live from simulated job activity via runDashboard.ts, including a real DLQ depth reading from Redis and correctly flipping to BREACHED. Rebuilt once after direct user feedback the first pass 'looks cheap': restructured into KPI summary / operational detail / needs-attention layers with real states (healthy/warning/critical/no-data/offline), a real recent-activity sparkline (not fabricated 24h/7d ranges, since nothing persists metrics), and reusable card-rendering functions. Two real bugs found and fixed in review: a raw negative error-budget percentage (-173%) displayed instead of clamping to 0%, and a missing <meta viewport> tag that silently broke all responsive behavior on mobile (verified via actual window.innerWidth, not just a screenshot). 76/76 tests passing, tsc --noEmit clean, zero browser console errors at desktop/tablet/mobile.

criteria.text: Given job load increases, When workers are needed, Then they are autoscaled
Given job load decreases, When workers are not needed, Then they are scaled down
Trust: Autoscaling events are logged with correlation IDs

stories.notes: Autoscaler scales real worker OS processes (ProcessWorkerPool forks workerProcess.ts, each running the standing consumer loop STORY-002 deferred) on real queue depth - the Redis consumer group's lag via queue.getBacklog(), not XLEN. Scale-up is immediate (criterion 1); scale-down waits until the backlog has stayed low for scaleDownAfter evaluations so a brief lull doesn't kill workers (criterion 2). Every scaling evaluation gets a fresh correlation ID that is logged on autoscale_up/autoscale_down/autoscale_down_deferred and passed to each spawned worker, which logs worker_started/worker_stopped with it (trust). Failure paths: unreadable or hung backlog read holds the current count and logs (never guesses 0); pool throw logs autoscale_failed and retries next evaluation; partial spawn logs autoscale_shortfall; a worker ignoring SIGTERM is force-killed after a grace period; a worker that dies on its own is logged and replaced on the next evaluation; a throwing logger never blocks a scaling decision and is counted in status().logFailures. Verified: integration test against real Redis 7.4 and real forked processes - 40 jobs enqueued, scaled 1 -> 4 separate live PIDs, all 40 processed exactly once, every scaled-up worker confirmed as a live consumer on the group via XINFO CONSUMERS, scaled back to 1 with the stopped PIDs confirmed dead and each having exited gracefully. Mutation check: forcing desiredWorkerCount to always 1 failed 12 tests. 100/100 tests passing three runs in a row, tsc --noEmit clean. Demo (npx tsx runAutoscaler.ts --quiet): 120-job burst scaled 1 -> 6, drained, deferred twice, scaled 6 -> 1. Limitation: each worker's idempotency store is in-process; correct today because a consumer group delivers each entry to one consumer, but cross-process duplicate protection on redelivery needs a shared store (STORY-008). Autoscaler runs on one host; scaling across machines is STORY-010's deploy concern. Follow-up 2026-10-22: removed a timing-dependent 'more than one worker processed jobs' assertion that flaked about 1 in 5 full-suite runs (the warm worker can drain ~1ms jobs before new ones boot), replaced with the XINFO CONSUMERS check; 10/10 full-suite runs pass.

criteria.text: Given a low-confidence job, When it is processed, Then it is routed to the review queue
Given a review queue, When a job is added, Then it is logged with a correlation ID
Trust: Low-confidence jobs are logged with correlation IDs

stories.notes: Low-confidence jobs (confidence < LOW_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD, now defined once in confidence.ts) are routed by jobRouter.ts to a separate review stream instead of being processed, and never to the DLQ (REQ-010). The review entry preserves the original job whole plus reason, confidence, threshold and routedAt. Wired into the worker loop and worker processes from STORY-006 (review stream defaults to '<stream>:review'). Criterion 1: routed to the review queue, verified against real Redis via peek() (XRANGE). Criterion 2: job_routed_to_review logged with the job's correlation ID and the review message id. Trust: the low-confidence job's own trail is job_low_confidence, job_dequeued, job_routed_to_review, all under one correlation ID. Failure paths: job does not route (review stream unwritable) retries 3 times with backoff, then falls back to the DLQ tagged review_queue_unavailable so it is neither lost nor resolved, and throws ReviewRouteFailedError if no DLQ is configured; the worker loop logs worker_job_unplaced and keeps running. Entry not logged: covered by the logging assertions. Auto-resolved: processJob itself now refuses low-confidence jobs (returns needs_review, logs job_not_auto_resolved, leaves the idempotency key unclaimed), so no other caller can resolve one either. Contract change: endToEnd.test.ts previously asserted a low-confidence job came back 'processed'; that is the behavior REQ-010 forbids, so it now expects needs_review. Verified: 109/109 tests, 10 consecutive full-suite runs, tsc --noEmit clean. Mutation checks: disabling routing failed 4 tests, removing the processJob guard failed 2. Demo (npx tsx src/runReviewRouting.ts): 6 jobs, the 3 below 0.5 in the review queue unresolved, 0.50 exactly processed, DLQ 0. Not built: a reviewer workflow to resolve review entries, and the MCP server's relay://jobs/needs-review resource still serves fixture data rather than reading this stream.

criteria.text: Given a DLQ entry, When it is triaged, Then the retry policy is updated
Given the retry policy, When a job fails, Then it follows the updated policy
Trust: DLQ triage updates are logged with correlation IDs

stories.notes: The DLQ runbook's Step 2 table is now code. failureClassifier.ts classifies a failure (live error by name, HTTP status or wrapped cause; DLQ reason by pattern) into timeout / client_error / upstream_error / review_queue_unavailable / unclassified. retryPolicy.ts holds one rule per class plus the codified triage rules: client_error in the DLQ switches the class to discard; timeout or upstream_error doubles that class's base backoff, capped at 10s; unclassified never changes the policy. INITIAL_POLICY reproduces pre-STORY-008 retry counts (verified by test). The policy lives in Redis (retryPolicyStore.ts) so all worker processes share it, with optimistic WATCH/MULTI updates, a bounded history of every change, and validation of the stored value. Criterion 1: triageNextDlqEntry (dlqTriage.ts) classifies a DLQ entry, updates the persisted policy, then resubmits (same idempotency key), discards, or escalates it; a job resubmitted more than twice is escalated. Criterion 2: withReliability takes the policy and follows the failed class's rule (attempts and backoff), with maxRetries still the hard ceiling; end-to-end test: a 400 job retried 3x into the DLQ, triage updated the policy, the next 400 job failed after 1 attempt. Trust: dlq_entry_classified, retry_policy_updated (with from/to rule and versions) and the outcome event all carry the entry's correlation ID; the policy's history also records it. Failure paths: not codified (unknown reason) escalates, never guesses; policy not updated (Redis down) returns the entry to the DLQ untouched and logs retry_policy_update_failed; concurrent triagers on separate connections both land (tested: 3 updates, version 4, no lost update); corrupt stored policy is never used on read or as an update base. Verified: 142/142 tests on 10 consecutive full-suite runs (33 new), tsc --noEmit clean. Mutation checks: disabling the client_error rule failed 7 tests, making withReliability ignore the policy failed 4. Demo (npx tsx src/runDlqTriage.ts): 400/503/unknown jobs dead-lettered under v1, triage discarded/resubmitted/escalated them and moved policy to v3, then a new 400 job failed after 1 attempt instead of 3. Runbook updated (automated triage section, what still needs a human). Limitations: no standing triage worker (triage is called by code); the STORY-006 worker loop doesn't make external calls, so policy-driven retries apply where callExternalApiAndPersist is given a retryPolicy; a DLQ reason that lost its HTTP status and has no recognisable text classifies as unclassified and goes to a human.

criteria.text: Given a chaos drill, When a worker is killed mid-job, Then the system recovers without data loss
Given a queue backlog, When it is forced, Then the system processes jobs without duplicates
Trust: Chaos drill events are logged with correlation IDs

stories.notes: Fixed the gap that made this story's first criterion impossible: jobs were acked on delivery, so a worker killed mid-job lost its job. Workers now read without acking (queue.readNew), ack only after the job is handled, and take over work a dead worker left pending (queue.reclaimStale, XAUTOCLAIM, with delivery counts from XPENDING). A message delivered more than maxDeliveries times goes to the DLQ (max_deliveries_exceeded) instead of crashing workers forever. Duplicate protection is now shared across worker processes (RedisIdempotencyStore, SET NX with 7-day expiry; processJobDurable), closing STORY-006's per-process limitation. The drill (chaosDrill.ts, runner runChaosDrill.ts, runbook docs/runbooks/CHAOS_DRILL.md) runs real forked worker processes against real Redis, forces a backlog including duplicate producer submissions, SIGKILLs workers while they hold a job (spread across the run), replaces them, and checks every job was processed exactly once. It refuses non-local Redis, uses drill-scoped keys, and always stops workers and deletes its keys. Criterion 1: kills land mid-job and a different worker handles the exact message the killed one held (matched by message id); 0 lost, 0 pending. Criterion 2: 120 jobs + 20 duplicate submissions processed exactly once, 20 skipped as duplicates; also holds under aggressive reclaim (reclaim 20ms < work 100ms, Drill B). Trust: chaos_drill_started / chaos_backlog_forced / chaos_fault_injected / chaos_worker_replaced / chaos_drill_completed all carry the drill's correlation ID, and each recovered job keeps its own correlation ID across workers (job_dequeued, job_reclaimed, job_processed / job_skipped_duplicate). Verified: drill A PASS x5 and drill B PASS x2 via npx tsx src/runChaosDrill.ts; drill shown to fail when protection is removed (ack-on-delivery: 2 lost, FAILED; per-process store under Drill B: 20 duplicates, FAILED), both reverted. 184/184 tests on 10 consecutive full-suite runs (7 new in chaos.test.ts incl. the drill itself, crash-after-claim-before-ack, poison message, cross-connection idempotency, non-local refusal), no orphan worker processes or leftover drill keys afterwards, tsc --noEmit clean. Limitations: Redis itself failing is not drilled (single Redis holds queue, DLQ, policy and idempotency keys; STORY-010); the idempotency claim is the commit point, so real side effects added to workers later must be keyed by the same idempotency key; no external-call faults inside workers yet.

criteria.text: Given the system is deployed, When it is running, Then job success rate and latency are tracked
Given the system is deployed, When a status request is made, Then a plain-language status view is provided
Trust: Given the system is running, Then monitoring data is logged for auditability

stories.notes: Relay is deployed to Fly.io (REQ-009): app relay-qn (https://relay-qn.fly.dev, one 512MB machine running src/server.ts: the autoscaler with 1-3 real worker processes, monitoring, and a read-only status server) and relay-qn-redis (private Redis 7.4, password from a Fly secret, append-only persistence on a 1GB volume, noeviction, IPv6 private network only). Estimated ~$6-8/month. Criterion 1: monitoring tracks success rate and p95 latency (end to end, from the stream id's enqueue time to job_processed in the workers' own logs) plus processed/failed counts, DLQ additions and depth, review routing and depth, queue depth and workers, sampled every 60s into a capped Redis stream (~7 days) readable at /metrics/history (REQ-014). Circuit breaker trips are recorded as null: the worker path makes no external calls, so nothing was measured. Criterion 2: /status is a plain-language page for analysts (REQ-013), /status.json the same with raw numbers. Trust: every sample is logged as metrics_sample with its own correlation ID, and the stored sample carries the same id. Failure paths: deployment fails (scripts/deploy.sh gates on type-check and full test suite, deploys one machine, smoke-checks the public URL, rolls back to the previous image on failure); monitoring service unavailable (sampler logs monitoring_sample_failed; status page says the queue can't be reached and shows no numbers, HTTP 503, while /health stays 200 so Fly doesn't restart-loop); status view not updated (samples older than 3 intervals are labelled out of date with their age). Verified in production: 200 jobs submitted via fly ssh, 192 processed at 100% success (p95 674ms) and 8 low-confidence routed to review, shown on the live status page; a 3000-job burst scaled workers 1 to 3 and back to 1 with autoscale events logged by correlation ID; second deploy.sh run passed tests, deploy and smoke check (ready=200 state=ok) with the previous image recorded for rollback. Locally: 200/200 tests on 3 runs (16 new), tsc clean, Redis-paused drill showed down/503 and self-recovery, Docker image and Redis image tested (unauthenticated clients refused, noeviction, password redacted in logs). Mutation checks: removing the stale check failed 1 test, removing the history write failed 2. Found during deploy: first smoke check falsely failed because this machine's DNS had cached 'not found' for the hostname from a pre-creation check; deploy.sh now resolves via public DNS and pins the IP. setup-fly.sh's secret check parsed Fly's table output and would have rotated the password on re-run; now uses JSON. Limitations: no alerting; rollback has been exercised only in its 'no previous image' branch, not a full bad-deploy drill; single Redis machine, no replica; no CI/CD (deploys from a laptop, still test-gated).

criteria.text: Given a classification task, When it is executed, Then it uses the fixed taxonomy
Given a classification task, When the taxonomy is unavailable, Then the task fails gracefully
Trust: Given a classification task, Then its execution is logged with the taxonomy version

stories.notes: The taxonomy is a versioned file (taxonomies/industry.v1.json, 12 industry codes) and the loader (taxonomy.ts) refuses any file whose SHA-256 or version doesn't match the pin in code, so 'fixed' is enforced: an edited file fails loudly instead of silently changing the labels. classifyJob.ts shows the classifier only the taxonomy's labels and rejects any label not in it (exact match), and any confidence outside 0..1. Criterion 1: classifier called with exactly the taxonomy labels, result accepted only from it; tested with the real pinned file. Criterion 2: missing, changed (hash or version) or malformed taxonomy fails with reason taxonomy_unavailable before the classifier is called; a failed load isn't cached, so a restored file works on the next task. Trust: classification_completed / classification_failed logged with the job's correlation ID and taxonomy id, version and sha256; the result also carries them. Failure paths: taxonomy not found (above); classification task fails (classifier errors retried with cap then classifier_failed; hang cut off by timeout; empty input rejected without a call); logging service unavailable: logger.ts no longer throws when the output stream is broken, it counts the lost line (getDroppedLogCount), and classification still completes with its audit fields on the result. Also: the taxonomy now owns the review threshold (reviewThreshold in the file); a classified job carries it and STORY-007's routing uses it instead of the global 0.5 placeholder, which remains only as a fallback. Verified: 165/165 tests on 5 consecutive full-suite runs (22 new classification + 1 logger), guardrails package 16/16, tsc --noEmit clean. Mutation checks: removing the label check failed 2 tests, removing the hash check failed 1. Demo (npx tsx src/runClassification.ts): 2 classified, 1 low-confidence flagged for review, invented label crypto_web3 rejected, missing taxonomy fails gracefully. Limitation: no real LLM or vendor classifier is wired in; the classifier is injected (keyword stand-in in the demo).

criteria.text: Given a summary is generated, When source data is available, Then it is grounded in that data
Given a summary is generated, When source data is missing, Then the summary generation fails
Trust: Given a summary is generated, Then its source data is logged for verification

stories.notes: summarizeJob.ts enforces REQ-016 by order: fetch the item's source (no source, no summary: the summarizer is never called), archive the exact source text by SHA-256 (sourceArchive.ts, Redis, content-addressed, 30-day TTL, tamper-checked on read), summarize from that text only, then check the summary with the existing grounding guardrail (guardrails/groundingGuardrail.ts, its first real caller). A summary that fails (low overlap, a number not in the source, empty) is never returned: it goes to the STORY-007 review queue as ungrounded_summary with its violations and source reference. Criterion 1: summarizer called with exactly the source text; grounded summaries returned with the source reference; ungrounded ones rejected and routed. Criterion 2: missing or blank source fails as source_missing, an unreachable or hanging source fails as source_unavailable after capped retries, summarizer never called in either case. Trust: summary_generated / summary_rejected_ungrounded / summary_failed logged with the job's correlation ID and the source's id, SHA-256 and length; verifySummary re-checks a summary against the archived source from the logged hash alone. Failure paths: source unavailable (above); summary generation fails (summarizer errors retried then summarizer_failed with the source reference; source can't be archived fails before summarizing rather than producing an unverifiable summary; review queue down falls back to the DLQ); logging unavailable: summary still completes and the result carries the source reference, dropped lines counted. Verified: 177/177 tests on 5 consecutive full-suite runs (12 new, against real Redis), guardrails 16/16, tsc --noEmit clean. Mutation checks: skipping the grounding check failed 4 tests, allowing a blank source failed 1. Demo (npx tsx src/runSummaries.ts): 1 grounded and re-verified from the archive, 1 rejected for an invented number, 1 rejected for drifting off the source, 1 failed for missing source. Limitations: the grounding guardrail is lexical (word overlap + numbers), so a summary that reuses the source's words but changes their meaning can pass; no real LLM summarizer or source fetcher is wired in (both injected).
